S No  and Registrar's  order with  Signatures  12.11.2024 Bail Application (IA No.01 of 2024)
 IN  CRLA No. 454 of 2024  Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Nandan Arya, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Mr. Sachin Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. This is an admitted appeal, admitted on 14.08.2024.
Trial Court record has been received, and paper-book is also prepared and supplied to learned counsels for the parties.
4. Heard on the bail application.

5. Present appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 29.07.2024, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Almora in Sessions Trial No.13 of 2022, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(1) read with Section 511 of IPC and sentenced to undergo five years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 50,000/- and in case of default of payment, to undergo additional rigorous imprisonment of six months.

The appellant was further convicted for the offence punishable under Section 354 of IPC and sentenced to undergo two years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.20,000/- and in case of default of payment, to undergo additional rigorous imprisonment for three months.

He was further convicted for the offence punishable under Section 323 of IPC and sentenced to undergo one year's simple imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/- and in case of default of payment, to undergo additional simple imprisonment for one week.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was on bail during trial, and he never misused the same.
Earlier he was in custody for about 11 months.

After conviction, he is in jail,
and he has served the sentence for about one year and two months.

Apart from this, the present appellant has no previous criminal antecedents CRLA/454/2024 on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115428035/
1
7. Learned State Counsel has not disputed this fact that the appellant was on bail during trial, and he has no previous criminal antecedents.

8. After taking into consideration that the appellant was on bail during trial, and has never misused the same, and since this appeal is of the year 2024, there is no possibility that the appeal be expedited shortly, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant deserves bail.
9. After taking into consideration the fact that the appellant is on bail during trial and he never misused the same, this Court is of the view that appellant deserved for bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, bail application is allowed.

11. Let appellant - Jagdish @Pappu be released on bail, during the pendency of the instant appeal,
on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties, each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
Realization of the fine imposed by the trial court shall also remain stayed.
12. It is made clear that if the appellant found to be indulged in any crixminal activity, the prosecution and the complainant are free to approach this Court for cancellation of bail.
Apart from this, the appellant shall also report his presence to the nearest police station on the first day of every month.
13. List this case for final hearing in the month of August, 2025.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 12.11.2024
NISHANT

on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115428035/
